chapters.hook: A familiar limps in off the north road, and the stall's herbs are not what the paw wants. Luke is already taking off his hat.
chapters.outcome: The hat carries the patient home; the red bed gives what the paw asks for, and it heals. The hat keeps its dent. His ledger line for the week: '...the dent stays. On purpose.'

chapters.hook: The familiars refuse the blue herb twice, and Luke is asked what they do want. He says nothing, which everyone present takes for an agreement to find out.
chapters.outcome: He waits; then the familiar leads him past the stall beds, past the good labels, to a far patch the tastings missed, and the tea is made from that. He does not label any of it. Ledger line: '...no labels needed, apparently.'

chapters.hook: The old dog's winter is a long one this year, and yellow herb can help - weakly, steadily, the way an old dog prefers its help. Luke starts the kettle.
chapters.outcome: He mixes the tea the weak way, because strong and sudden is for emergencies and this is neither. One line goes on the stall door: 'Every evening. Even when it rains.' The dog agrees by sleeping closer, and the line is never taken down.

chapters.hook: Someone small wants the high shelf, and the only ladder in the shop has rules attached to it. Luke goes to look at the sturdy caps instead.
chapters.outcome: Sturdy caps, wide as saucers, make fine stairs; he counts them twice and leaves the third alone, because a nest is holding its shadow there now. The mushroom-stairs last all spring, and one kitten approves - loudly, per his note: '...loudly.'

chapters.hook: Familiars have been answering voices that are not attached to anything, and the clever-mushroom patch is the prime suspect. Luke takes the case quietly.
chapters.outcome: The mushrooms copy familiar calls, but the copied voice is off; he finds the true cluster by sitting still until a call comes honestly. The imitation patch gets one small chalk line - nothing scary - and the familiars stop being fooled. Notebook entry: '...the chalk holds.'

chapters.hook: The young one is racing the roofline at dusk again, and the neighbors have begun learning its name by heart. Luke is considering one drop of tea.
chapters.outcome: One drop of lively-mushroom tea goes into the supper dish, and the quiet hour arrives on its own, surprised to be wanted. He writes the hour into every day after that; the young one forgives him by Tuesday, which he noted in advance: '...Tuesday.'

chapters.hook: Stall signs promise that fruit of power is good for every age, and one of the pets is young enough to believe a stall sign. Luke is not.
chapters.outcome: He keeps the fruit on the windowsill anyway and feeds soft mash instead, twice a day, saying nothing out loud about later. The promise holds; so does the note underneath the pot: '...patient fruit, he decides.'

chapters.hook: The talking-bird has been asking a single word since the wisdom fruit went near it, and the word is 'why.' The word is aimed directly at Luke.
chapters.outcome: It asked for three days straight; he trades riddles until the bird trades better, and the truce holds - mostly. The perch stays with the question, and the closing tally reads: '...a good word to have won.'

chapters.hook: The old dog's evening walks have been getting shorter by the week, and spirit fruit promises nothing it cannot keep. Luke cuts the slivers thin.
chapters.outcome: Thin slivers go into the evening bowl, and the slow walks get longer, street by street. Not healed - kinder. The ledger entries that week run three ellipses deep: '...good.'

chapters.hook: A fledgling is too light for wool bedding, and the autumn cold does not care about dignity. Luke goes gathering with a clean jar.
chapters.outcome: Rainbow down, washed soft, makes a nesting jar - shallow on purpose, so small birds can leave when they choose. One does, and comes back; that gets a second line in the ledger, the most the ledger has ever said: '...it came back.'

chapters.hook: The winter boxes keep losing heat at night, and Luke has heard of a bedding that sings about weather before the weather arrives. He is willing to listen.
chapters.outcome: Bluebird down sings when the cold comes - a thin note under the door, a chaperone for the frost - so he lines the winter boxes with it. The small ones sleep through their own warnings now, which is what bedding is for. Ledger note: '...hears the weather first.'

chapters.hook: The winter litter needs a den, and the wind has spent the month redesigning the garden. One old-shed feather is wider than the whole doorway.
chapters.outcome: Wyvern feather, taken with a permission that asked everyone including the wind; the winter litter sleeps under it, one piece. It keeps the frost out and - somehow - the fear out too. His note is the longest of the month: '...fear is smaller under big roofs.'

chapters.hook: Familiar eggs are due across the frost week, and Luke's own nesting corner has gone quiet in the wrong way. He has a hat, a stool, and the patience to sit through either.
chapters.text: The frost week: Luke watched the crag from the mill path with two familiars pretending to be rocks. He did not cross the tree line; the wild eggs were not his to keep, and his own familiar's eggs nested warm at home without coaxing. The roost stayed safe - that much the town knows - and the small cold birds on the mill roof voted to keep their opinions private. His only remark went home with him: '...some weeks, watching is the job.'
